title: Applied ML Eval Harness: Integrated Playbook for Prompt Sets, Model Onboarding, Quantization, and Regression Triage
author: Rina Patel
body:
Summary:

This playbook consolidates the Applied ML team’s standards and procedures for using the eval harness, maintaining curated prompt sets and benchmarks, onboarding new models, validating quantization profiles, and executing regression triage. It is intended for ML engineers, model owners, and SREs who operate Redwood’s inference-enabled products and model evaluation pipelines.

Goals:
- Provide a repeatable, auditable path for model onboarding and regression detection.
- Ensure prompt sets and benchmarks reflect production workloads and edge cases.
- Standardize quantization validation to guard against quality regressions.
- Define an actionable triage process that minimizes customer impact and time-to-fix.

Table of contents:
1) Roles & ownership
2) Eval harness pipeline overview
3) Model onboarding checklist
4) Prompt set and benchmark guidelines
5) Quality guardrails and thresholds
6) Quantization profile validation
7) Regression triage playbook
8) Metrics, dashboards, and alerts
9) Release and rollback guidance
10) References and templates

1) Roles & ownership
- Model Owner: responsible for model artifacts, onboarding checklist items, and remediation when regressions originate from model changes.
- Eval Engineer: maintains eval harness CI, implements prompt sets, and runs scheduled/regression jobs.
- Applied ML Lead: approves model signoffs and risk exceptions.
- SRE/Platform: ensures eval infrastructure availability and enforces resource quotas.
- Product QA: validates user-facing behavior where necessary.

2) Eval harness pipeline overview
The harness runs deterministic pipelines that produce reproducible evaluation reports. Key stages:
1. Ingest model bundle (artifact, version, quantization metadata).
2. Sanity checks: schema, tokenization roundtrip, sample generation smoke tests.
3. Run prompt-set based benchmarks (N prompt sets in parallel).
4. Compute metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/EM/Exact-Match for structured tasks, embedding similarity, hallucination rate, toxicity checks).
5. Compare to baseline and quantization-aware thresholds.
6. Produce HTML + JSON report and publish to eval dashboard.

Sample CI job (simplified):
``
jobs:
  run-eval:
    image: ruby:3.1
    steps:
      - checkout
      - run: bundle install
      - run: ./eval-harness/bin/run_eval --model $MODEL_BUNDLE --prompt-sets default,prod-edge --output ./reports/$MODEL_VERSION.json
```

3) Model onboarding checklist (required before canary/serving)
- Artifact: model bundle uploaded to artifact registry with immutable version tag.
- Metadata: architecture, tokenizer, sequence length, FLOPs estimate, supported precisions (fp16,int8/q4x), KVs support.
- Eval harness: successful run of full benchmark suite with metrics attached.
- Latency & perf: p50/p95 single-request latency meets target on intended instance types (see Performance SLO table below).
- Security & licensing: license compatibility checked; export controls documented.
- Rollout plan: canary shard percentage, fallback target models, rollback criteria.

Model onboarding acceptance table (example):
| Item | Owner | Criteria | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Artifact upload | Model Owner | Bundle present in registry | TODO |
| Tokenizer validation | Eval Engineer | Roundtrip passes on 1000 samples | TODO |
| Eval metrics | Eval Engineer | All critical metrics >= baseline thresholds | TODO |
| Perf | SRE | p95 <= 350ms on c6g/g5x profile | TODO |
| Security review | Security | No disallowed dependencies | TODO |

4) Prompt set and benchmark guidelines
- Prompt set taxonomy: production, adversarial, long-context, safety, few-shot templates. Each prompt set must include: description, intent, expected distribution, and coverage notes.
- Minimum size: production prompt sets should contain at least 1,000 anonymized examples representative of live traffic; adversarial sets should include targeted edge cases (100–500 examples).
- Labeling: where ground-truth exists, use blinded human labels with inter-annotator agreement (Cohen’s kappa > 0.6).
- Parameter sweep: benchmarks must be run at the same decoding settings used in production (temperature, top_k/top_p, max_tokens). Deviations must be documented.

Prompt set header (YAML example):
``
name: prod-completions-2026-q1
description: Representative completions from Product Search feature (anonymized)
size: 1450
tags: [production, completions, search]
expected_metrics: {perplexity: < 40, fluency: > 0.85}
```

5) Quality guardrails and thresholds
- Primary guardrails (per-model):
  - Fluency: human-rated fluent output >= 0.85 (0–1 scale).
  - Hallucination: <= 3% on fact-based prompt sets.
  - Toxicity: flagged outputs <= 0.5% per Safety API.
  - Regression delta: no metric regression > 3% relative to baseline for critical metrics.
- Canary thresholds: canary failure if any critical metric drops > 2% or error rates increase > 50% vs baseline.
- Approval process: models failing guardrails must be remediated or rollouts restricted to internal usage only.

6) Quantization profile validation
Objective: validate each quantization profile (e.g., q4_0, q8_0, int8 dynamic) to ensure acceptable quality drop and quantize-specific perf gains.
Validation steps:
1. Define baseline: FP16 or full-precision metrics on production prompt sets.
2. Run quantized model through full benchmark suite.
3. Compute delta per metric and aggregate quality score.
4. If any critical metric delta > configured threshold (default 3%), block automated rollout and escalate to applied-ml for review.
5. Document memory/latency improvements and annotate profile in model metadata.

Quantization acceptance table:
| Profile | p50 latency delta | Memory delta | Metric delta (max) | Accept? |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| q4_0 | -18% | -45% | 1.8% | YES |
| int8 | -32% | -60% | 4.5% | NO (requires review) |

7) Regression triage playbook
When an automated job or monitoring alert indicates a regression:
1. Triage: Eval Engineer reproduces regression locally with the exact model and prompt set version used by CI.
2. Scope: Determine affected prompt sets, metrics, and percentage deviation.
3. Root-cause hypothesis: model change, quantization, infra perf, tokenization change, or prompt drift.
4. Quick revert: If regression is severe (>5% critical metric delta or customer-facing error spike), initiate rollback to last-known-good model per rollback checklist.
5. Deep analysis: run diff tests, sample-level comparison, attention map snapshots (when available), and compare tokenization outputs.
6. Fix & validate: code/model fix or prompt set update; re-run harness; update release notes.
7. Postmortem: Document incident, RCA, and mitigations; update prompt sets or eval harness as needed.

Escalation matrix:
- Level 1: Eval Engineer (within 2 hours)
- Level 2: Applied ML Lead & SRE (within 6 hours)
- Level 3: Head of Engineering and Product (within 24 hours)

8) Metrics, dashboards, and alerts
Recommended dashboards (Redwood Console):
- Per-model benchmark overview: key metrics, trend lines, and quantization comparisons.
- Canary rollouts: canary vs baseline metric drift and error counts.
- Regression heatmap: prompt set x metric deltas across model versions.
- Perf vs cost: tokens/sec, cost-per-token by model and instance type.

Alerting thresholds (examples):
- Regression alert: critical metric delta > 3% over baseline for 3 consecutive CI runs.
- Perf degradation: p95 latency increase > 50ms vs baseline for 10 minutes.
- Error spike: error rate increase > 100% for request failures.

9) Release and rollback guidance
Release checklist (pre-canary):
- All onboarding items complete and green.
- Canary and fallback targets configured.
- Eval report published and reviewed by Applied ML Lead.
- Monitoring & alerts configured.

Rollback steps (quick):
1. Pause incoming traffic to canary route.
2. Switch traffic to fallback model/version via feature flag or routing policy.
3. Re-run failing CI jobs against fallback to confirm behavior.
4. Notify stakeholders and open incident if customer impact observed.

- prompt-set-header.yaml

Appendix: Example eval-report JSON (abbreviated)
``
{
  "model_version": "v2026-03-01-candidate",
  "prompt_sets": ["prod-completions-2026-q1", "safety-adversarial-2026"],
  "metrics": {"fluency": 0.88, "hallucination_rate": 0.024, "toxicity_rate": 0.002},
  "quantization_profile": "q4_0",
  "delta_vs_baseline": {"fluency": -0.01}
}
```

Notes and FAQs:
- When to accept small metric drops: Accept only if there is a measurable latency/cost tradeoff documented and product approves.
- Handling data drift: Prompt sets should be refreshed quarterly or when monitored distribution shift exceeds thresholds.

Contact and ownership:

- Eval harness repo: github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness
- For incidents: page the Applied ML on-call via PagerDuty (team: applied-ml)

This playbook is reviewed quarterly and updated when new quantization methods or evaluation metrics are introduced.
